article_title: Theoretical Perspectives on Teaching with Robots: From Interdisciplinary Prerequisites and Necessities in Today’s Classrooms to Five Different Types of Robots
citation: Christ, O., Riedl, R., Schmid, J., Zürcher, P., & Thilo, F. (2026). Theoretical Perspectives on Teaching with Robots: From Interdisciplinary Prerequisites and Necessities in Today's Classrooms to Five Different Types of Robots. AI Educ. 2, 28. https://doi.org/10.3390/aieduc2030028
title: 4E cognition framework as a heuristic for designing embodied learning technology
description: The article presents 4E cognition as a framework in which cognition is 'not solely a brain-based process, but is also influenced by the body, the environment, and interactions'. Its four dimensions—embodied, embedded, enacted, and extended—are used to explain how learning is distributed across bodies, tools, and social environments, and to map design features of social robots onto learning processes. The authors position MindMatters as an applied instantiation of 4E principles.
requirements: Learning environments must incorporate interactive elements and real-world engagement for the framework to apply to technology-enhanced learning
constraints: Critics argue the approach sometimes blurs the boundaries of cognition, making it difficult to delineate what constitutes cognitive processes
target_learners: school students in primary and secondary education
examples: The article maps each 4E dimension onto general design features of social robots, e.g. embodied cognition reflected in robots enabling physical interaction and sensorimotor engagement
key_sources: Christ, O., Riedl, R., Schmid, J., Zürcher, P., & Thilo, F. (2026). Theoretical Perspectives on Teaching with Robots: From Interdisciplinary Prerequisites and Necessities in Today's Classrooms to Five Different Types of Robots. AI Educ. 2, 28. https://doi.org/10.3390/aieduc2030028

article_title: The influence of physical activity on the creativity of 10 and 11-year-old school children
citation: Romance, R., Nielsen-Rodríguez, A., Sousa Mendes, R., Dobado-Castañeda, J. C., & Dias, G. (2023). The influence of physical activity on the creativity of 10 and 11-year-old school children. Thinking Skills and Creativity. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tsc.2023.101295
title: 4E cognition approach to creativity (embodied, embedded, enactive, extended)
description: The article adopts an embodied account in which "creative development happens as a result of the acting on and within an environment". The 4E cognition approach holds that, beyond idea generation, "the role of creative cognition is to guide action", treating human cognition as a dynamical system encompassing brain/mind, body and world/environment including objects, materials and artifacts. On this view, how we learn and develop expertise is shaped, constrained and enacted through exploration and interaction with the physical environment, which motivates studying physical activity as an environmental factor in children's creative development.
requirements: Adopting this account requires treating body movement and physical environment interaction as active components of creative cognition, not merely background variables.
constraints: The article notes few creativity theories still incorporate the embodied aspect, and that specific pedagogical practices leading to creativity have not been identified.
target_learners: Children in the last cycle of primary education (10–11 years old)
target_learning_goals: Development of creative thinking and divergent-thinking capacities
examples: The study operationalises the embodied account by measuring children's daily physical activity with triaxial accelerometry and relating it to Torrance Test divergent-thinking dimensions.
key_sources: Romance, R., Nielsen-Rodríguez, A., Sousa Mendes, R., Dobado-Castañeda, J. C., & Dias, G. (2023). The influence of physical activity on the creativity of 10 and 11-year-old school children. Thinking Skills and Creativity. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tsc.2023.101295

article_title: Toward a unified vocabulary for embodiment research challenges and solutions
citation: Peng Wang, Jingming Li, Qian Yu, Liye Zou, Xia Xu, Myrto Mavilidi, Ryan S. Falck, Fabian Herold, Robert J. Schinke, Markus Raab & Fred Paas. (2026). Toward a unified vocabulary for embodiment research: challenges and solutions. npj Science of Learning 11:36. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00413-x
title: 4E cognition as an umbrella framework grouping Embodied, Embedded, Enactive, and Extended approaches
description: The article presents the 4E cognition approach as an integrative framework grouping Embodied, Embedded, Enactive, and Extended ideas under one umbrella, explicitly acknowledging the multifaceted nature of cognitive systems. It advocates that cognition is "shaped and structured by dynamic interactions between the brain, body, and both the physical and social environments". The authors use it as a broad definition many subfields can agree on, while noting fragmentation persists within 4E because its traditions diverge at the level of ontology and explanation.
requirements: A shared glossary should map terms to their core claims, typical operationalizations, and underlying commitments while noting where positions are genuinely incommensurable
constraints: The 4E umbrella brings together traditions that sometimes diverge at the level of ontology and explanation, e.g., enactivist approaches foreground autonomy and sense-making while many embodied or grounded cognition strands use representational sensorimotor simulations
target_learners: researchers and students across psychology, neuroscience, education, AI, and public health
target_learning_goals: understanding how body, brain, and environment interact in cognition and learning
examples: The article defines embodiment as an umbrella term with sub-terms like embodied (body-focused) and embedded (environment-focused), building on the 4E cognition framework
key_sources: Peng Wang, Jingming Li, Qian Yu, Liye Zou, Xia Xu, Myrto Mavilidi, Ryan S. Falck, Fabian Herold, Robert J. Schinke, Markus Raab & Fred Paas. (2026). Toward a unified vocabulary for embodiment research: challenges and solutions. npj Science of Learning 11:36. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00413-x

article_title: Convincing Science Teachers for Inquiry-Based Instruction: Guskey's Staff Development Model Revisited
citation: Zambak, V. S., Alston, D. M., Marshall, J. C., & Tyminski, A. M. (2017). Convincing Science Teachers for Inquiry-Based Instruction: Guskey's Staff Development Model Revisited. Science Educator, 25(2), 108-116. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1143566
title: 4Ex2 Instructional Model
description: The planning model that the PD program encouraged teachers to use was the 4Ex2 Instructional Model (Marshall, Horton, & Smart, 2009), an adaptation of the 5E Instructional Model (Bybee et al., 2006). The 4Ex2 Model uses the following instructional sequence: Engage, Explore, Explain, and Extend. The "x2" stands for the continuous formative assessment and teacher reflection that should occur throughout each of the four stages.
requirements: The model requires continuous formative assessment and teacher reflection throughout each of the four stages.
examples: The 4Ex2 Model uses the following instructional sequence: Engage, Explore, Explain, and Extend.
key_sources: Zambak, V. S., Alston, D. M., Marshall, J. C., & Tyminski, A. M. (2017). Convincing Science Teachers for Inquiry-Based Instruction: Guskey's Staff Development Model Revisited. Science Educator, 25(2), 108-116. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1132092

article_title: The links between experiential learning and 4E cognition.
citation: Lebert, A., & Vilarroya, Ó. (2024). The links between experiential learning and 4E cognition. Ann NY Acad Sci, 1541, 37–52. https://doi.org/10.1111/nyas.15238
title: 4E cognition framework: embodied, embedded/situated, extended, and enactive approaches to cognition
description: 4E cognition is an umbrella term for approaches sharing the idea that intelligent behavior cannot be understood solely by examining internal brain processes; cognition emerges from neural and bodily activities interacting with the environment in context. The article names four schools: "embodied cognition, situated cognition, the extended‐mind thesis, and enactivism, hence the four “e” in 4E cognition". It lists central assumptions including that cognition is situated in physical and social contexts, enacted for action, distributed across material and social settings, and often requires no explicit internal mental representation.
requirements: Cognition must be characterized by integrating neural and bodily activities with the environment and context, not by studying the brain alone
constraints: The article notes there are no well-established boundaries clearly distinguishing the four schools; the distinctions must be taken as loose
target_learners: general readers of cognitive neuroscience and educational psychology
target_learning_goals: understanding how cognition relates to body, environment, and action
examples: The article uses the four schools section by section to map links to experiential learning: embodied, situated, extended, and enactive connections.
key_sources: Lebert, A., & Vilarroya, Ó. (2024). The links between experiential learning and 4E cognition. Ann NY Acad Sci, 1541, 37–52. https://doi.org/10.1111/nyas.15238
